look_here_first: Look DOWN at the basal ROSETTE before checking flowers. Mature S. lyrata leaves are LYRATE: a larger rounded TERMINAL lobe toward the leaf tip and smaller paired LATERAL lobes closer to the stalk; some leaves vary from shallow to deeply cut. A mostly leafless square flowering stalk rises well above, bearing SMALL lavender-blue bilabiate flowers in widely spaced tiers. Cedar sage also forms a rosette, but often has separate 1–3 leaflets with long petioles and CRIMSON corollas. Do not rely on basal rosette alone.
project_tracker_diagnostic: perennial basal rosette; lyrate/pinnatifid basal leaves; flowering stems rise well above rosette; small blue-lavender bilabiate flowers in spaced verticils; often in low moist/open woods, meadows, disturbed ground

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Wildflower Center printable Hays County native list / NPSOT Hill Country compilation. Travis — Travis County/Texas A&M Urban Programs treats Salvia lyrata as an Austin-area native plant; additional county-voucher confirmation is still desirable. Kew confirms the species is native in Texas, but a third explicit project-target county native occurrence has not yet been documented to the project standard.

morphology_keys.basal_leaf_structure: Lyrate/pinnatifid basal leaves: broad rounded end (terminal) lobe and smaller side lobes, often separated by narrow sinus; leaf remains ONE continuous blade, not several detached leaflets.
morphology_keys.flowering_axis: Usually mostly leafless above rosette, tall unbranched or sparsely branched square stem with spaced verticils of pale blue/lavender two-lipped flowers.
morphology_keys.habit: Herbaceous perennial with flat basal rosette, unlike woody branching greggii/ballotiflora; green or purplish winter rosettes may persist.
morphology_keys.lookalike_cedar: Cedar sage also low rosette, but broad petiolate leaves can be 1–3 FOLIOLATE (separate lateral leaflets), and crimson flowers in woodland shade; lyreleaf has a lyrately LOBED single blade and pale blue flowers. Leaf shape/calyx support identification.
morphology_keys.leaf_variation: Entire to shallowly lobed leaves and purple-stained cultivated forms occur; don't claim every plant has deeply cut lobes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Salvia roemeriana: Both can form basal rosettes. Lyreleaf sage has the characteristic deeply lyre-shaped rosette and small blue-lavender flowers; cedar sage has broader cordate/lyrate leaves and red flowers in shaded juniper habitat.

mini_glossary.lyrate: LYE-rate — broad rounded tip lobe with smaller side lobes, like a lyre outline
mini_glossary.lobe: Part of a SINGLE leaf blade separated by indentations, not a separate leaf
mini_glossary.leaflet: A SEPARATE blade of a compound leaf, attached to petiole or rachis
mini_glossary.rosette: A low circular cluster of leaves at the crown
mini_glossary.verticil: Flowers that appear grouped around a stem at one level
mini_glossary.bilabiate: A two-lipped flower with distinct upper and lower lips

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: LYRELEAF = ONE LOBED blade, LAVENDER flowers, LEAFLESS stalk; CEDAR = possible separate leaflets, CRIMSON flowers.
